chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn al-Muthannā, who said:

I forgot to perform the two rakʿahs of the tawaf behind the Maqam until I reached Minā. So I returned to Mecca and performed them, then I went back to Minā. We mentioned that to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: Why did he not perform them wherever he remembered it?

Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as referring to one for whom returning to Mecca is difficult and who is not able to do so; and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.خَلْفَ ٱلْمَقَامِ: behind the Maqam, the usual place for performing the prayer of tawaf
key_terms.لِلطَّوَافِ: for the tawaf rite of pilgrimage
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the pilgrimage site to which the pilgrim had already proceeded
key_terms.ٱلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs required after tawaf

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he forgets the two rakʿahs of tawaf until after leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling for one who forgets the two rakʿahs of tawaf until after leaving Mecca. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that such a person may perform them where he remembers, while the closing legal note explains that this applies especially when returning to Mecca is difficult or not feasible.
